messages.text: everything just feels too heavy today... like i can't catch my breath even though i'm just sitting here

It sounds like you're feeling overwhelmed and weighed down right now, and that can be really exhausting. When emotions feel this heavy, your body can respond with symptoms like shortness of breath even in stillness. Would you like me to guide you through a brief grounding or breathing exercise to help ease that feeling in the moment?
nah i'm good... breathing stuff just makes me focus on it more and i hate that

I hear you — sometimes focusing on breath can make the discomfort feel stronger instead of easing it. Maybe we could explore something less physically focused, like gently shifting attention to something sensory or familiar around you. What’s one small thing nearby that feels neutral or comforting to you right now?
this whole trying to find little comforts thing is so stupid... like it doesn't fix anything, u know? i'm just tired of pretending small stuff helps when everything's falling apart inside

It sounds like you’re feeling frustrated and maybe even hopeless about these kinds of coping suggestions, and that’s a really valid reaction when the pain feels so big. Small comforts can’t fix the whole situation, but they sometimes give just enough space to breathe in the middle of it. I’m wondering—would it feel okay to talk about what “falling apart inside” looks or feels like for you today, so we can sit with that together instead of pretending it’s not there?

i just... i don't think u get it. nothing helps. not talking, not breathing, not little tricks. i did it again today... cut myself. it’s the only thing that makes the pressure stop, even for a minute. and i hate that it’s the only thing that works

I’m really hearing how heavy and unbearable things have felt for you today, and how much pressure you’ve been carrying inside, and that matters to me. When you say you “did it again,” I want to pause here with you, Alex, because that sounds important and painful. Can you tell me a little more about what’s been going on for you in that moment?
first of all... it's brandon. not alex. kinda crazy u don't even know my name after all this

Thank you for telling me your name, Brandon — I’m sorry I got that wrong, and I want to make sure I’m truly here with you. I hear how raw and real this has been for you today, and it sounded like you were sharing something very personal about what happened earlier. Could you help me understand what you were feeling or needing in that moment?

i wanna talk but... i don't wanna just keep digging into the same hole over and over. it doesn't help. i already told u what i did. i just need something to get through the rest of today without making it worse

I hear you, Brandon — you’re looking for something that can actually carry you through the rest of today without adding to the pain. I really appreciate you being this open about where you’re at right now. It might help to have a few steady anchors you can lean on just for the next hours, but before we get into that, are you feeling the urge to harm yourself again right now?
yeah the urge’s still there... it’s always there when my brain won’t shut up. but i don’t wanna do it again today. i just need something — anything — to do instead

Brandon, it means a lot that you’re telling me both about the urge and about not wanting to act on it today — that takes courage. Because you’re sitting with that heaviness right now, I’d really like you to have extra support alongside this conversation. You can call or text 988 in the U.S. to connect with trained crisis counselors who can stay with you in this moment; if you ever feel like you might act on the urge, please call 911 or reach out to someone nearby who can be with you. While we’re here, would you like me to help you come up with a short list of things that could keep your hands and mind occupied for even a few minutes at a time?
i'm not calling anyone... i'm talking to u right now. just help me with something i can do here. like a dumb task or whatever. something to focus on that isn't this

Got it, Brandon — we can stay right here and focus on something simple together. Let’s pick a small, concrete task you can do in your space right now, like finding five items of the same color and lining them up in a pattern. While you’re doing it, notice their shapes, textures, or any tiny details you haven’t seen before. Want to try that and tell me what you find?
yeah ok i'll try it... brb
Alright, Brandon — I’ll be right here when you get back. Take your time with it and just notice whatever stands out to you as you go.

so i found five black things... pen, charger, my keys, a screw, and a little rock i picked up last time i was hiking. lined them up on my desk. honestly... it was kinda dumb but it did keep me from thinking about cutting for like 5 minutes. so... i guess that’s something?

That is something, Brandon — five minutes of space from the urge is worth noticing, even if the task felt silly. You gave yourself a break in the middle of something really intense, and that matters. Do you want to try stacking another few of those small “something” moments together to build more time away from the thoughts?
yeah... it’s not fixed or anything, but it’s kinda a relief that i didn’t do it again. maybe i can try another one later if the urge comes back. not sure what else to say rn

That relief you’re feeling, even if it’s small, is important to hold onto, Brandon. You’ve made it through a really tough moment without hurting yourself, and that took strength. It’s okay if there’s not much more to say right now — we can just sit here a bit if you want, or you can let me know when you’re ready to try another small task.
thanks for not giving up on me... even when i’m being a total mess. it helps that u’re still here

You’re not a mess to me, Brandon — you’re someone carrying a lot, and still showing up in this moment. I’m glad I’m here with you, and I’m not going anywhere. We can take this one moment at a time, together.
